title: Finite evaluation of the ordinary system open counit
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, an open immersion j:X→Y, an ordinary system open extension o as in [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and a nonnegative coefficient index n. There is a finite left adjoint L to the specified finite inverse image, with adjunction adj, and a natural isomorphism e:o.ordinary ev_Y,n ≅ ev_X,n L. For every system N on Y, evaluation of o.adjunction.counit at N equals e at the system inverse image of N, followed by L applied to the inverse of the specified inverse-image/evaluation comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], followed by adj.counit at ev_Y,n(N). This assertion has no completed coefficient module, ordinary reduction functor or reconstruction model as input.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, open-factor normalization: the ordinary section-normalized quotient/open map.

proof.text: Specialize the existing varying-ring operations to the actual positive quotient rings ULift(O_E/varpi^(n+1)) and their quotient maps. The sequence module categories and their evaluation functors are definitionally the recorded coefficientSequenceModules and coefficientSequenceEvaluation. Uniqueness of the section-normalized sequence ring map identifies pullbackTensorSequenceDirect with the varying-ring pushforward. The adjunction transpose identity identifies the finite right adjoint with the standard constant-ring direct image.

The actual direct-image evaluation comparison is the varying-ring moduleEvalP: both maps are identity on every section, so function extensionality and the existing module-functor isomorphism extensionality theorem identify them. Let q be the unit-preserving uniqueness isomorphism from the specified finite inverse image to the standard constant-ring inverse image. Transposing under the finite adjunction, its unit identity and the unit equation for moduleEvalG show that the specified inverse-image/evaluation comparison is evaluation whiskered with q followed by moduleEvalG inverse. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves equality of the natural isomorphisms. This uses the actual normalization, not an arbitrary comparison.

Use the proved ordinaryOpenMateIso in VaryingRingOperations. Transport its invertibility to the supplied ordinary open extension by leftAdjointUniq and mateEquiv_leftAdjointUniq. The inverse of this mate supplies e. Choose the standard finite open extension as L, with its open adjunction transported on the right through q inverse. The mate counit identity gives the evaluated system counit formula in standard finite coordinates. Substitute the comparison from the preceding step; functoriality cancels q inverse against q in the transported counit, giving exactly the asserted formula. All constructions are ordinary; no completed coefficients, derived objects, coefficient flatness or nonempty-open hypothesis is used.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryOpenFiniteEvaluation {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (o : Open l E j) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (L : normalizedDVRModules l E X n ⥤ normalizedDVRModules l E Y n)
      (adj : L ⊣ integralOperationsLevelPullback l E j n)
      (e : o.ordinary ⋙ coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n ≅
        coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n ⋙ L),
      ∀ N : coefficientSequenceModules l E Y,
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).map (o.adjunction.counit.app N) =
          e.hom.app ((pullbackTensorSequenceInverse l E j).obj N) ≫
            L.map ((pullbackTensorSequenceInverseEvaluation l E j n).inv.app N) ≫
            adj.counit.app ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).obj N)
